_comment: PLACEHOLDER FOR CI ONLY. Every value here is fake.
The real google-services.json is gitignored, so a CI runner has no Firebase
configuration and the Google Services Gradle plugin refuses to configure the
project at all: 'File google-services.json is missing.' That blocked the
Android build job outright, which meant the entire native surface of this app
stayed unverified for want of a config file.
The workflow copies this into place before building. What that verifies is
real: Gradle configuration, Kotlin and Java compilation, every native plugin,
R8 shrinking, and asset bundling. What it cannot verify is anything that talks
to Firebase, because none of these identifiers exist.
Which is why the CI job does not publish the APK it builds. An artifact with
this file baked in would look like a working build and fail at sign-in, and
someone would spend an afternoon on it. Build the shippable APK where the real
package_name must match applicationId in app/build.gradle.kts or the plugin
rejects the file. That is the one value here that is not arbitrary.
